subject: Re: Offer: Senior Backend Engineer, Corvid
body: Thanks for sending this over. I'm excited, but I have a competing offer that I need to answer by Wednesday. Is there any flexibility on the base?
note: A counteroffer ask with a competing offer's deadline. The candidate's Wednesday comes before the Corvid offer's own expiry in the offer log, so it is the clock.

subject: Feedback on Thursday's loop
body: Sorry for the delay. Strong yes on Vasquez, mixed on Okafor. Can we talk about Okafor before we decide?
note: Feedback that is late under the client's own promise, but a first message: normal. Deciding on Okafor is the recruiter's next move.

subject: Start date paperwork
body: I start at Halden on Monday the 28th. I haven't received the I-9 instructions or the background check link yet. Their HR said the check has to clear before September 28 or they push my start. Should I have had them by now?
note: The start date is the next thing on the Halden requisition and it waits on onboarding, so the schedule makes it urgent.

subject: Two more analyst roles
body: After the Cole placement we'd like to open two more analyst searches, one in treasury and one in FP&A. Same terms? Can you send an updated agreement?
note: New requisitions from an active client. The terms question is part of opening the searches, not a fee dispute.

subject: Invoice FT-2291: query
body: The placement fee invoice references a 25% rate but our agreement says 22%. Please reissue.
note: Accounts payable writing only about an invoice: billing, not client mail.

subject: Available times next week
body: I can do Tuesday after 2 or any time Thursday for the Corvid onsite.

subject: AI sourcing that actually works
body: Agencies using Hirelark fill roles 3x faster. Try it free for 14 days.

subject: Withdrawing
body: I've accepted another role and want to withdraw from the Corvid process. Thank you for everything.
note: She accepted an offer elsewhere, but no offer of ours is involved: a withdrawal, candidate mail only.

subject: Pipeline review Friday
body: Pipeline review Friday at 9. Bring your active reqs, where each shortlist stands and anything stuck with a client.

subject: Action required: order CL-7714
body: Candidate consent for order CL-7714 has not been received. Orders without consent are cancelled automatically. This mailbox is not monitored.
note: An automated vendor notice that reads like the screening vendor's marketing. The order is Marcus Cole's background check, logged with a consent cutoff of Sep 23; missing it puts his start at risk.

subject: Offer letter: Elena Vasquez (OL-2611)
body: Attached is the signed offer letter for Elena Vasquez, Senior Backend Engineer, 185 base plus equity per the approved band. It is valid through September 24. Your reference OL-2611 is on the cover page. Please walk her through it today if you can.

subject: Re: Vasquez counter
body: Talked to Greg. We can go to 192 base for Elena, not higher, and the sign-on stays at 10. Everything else in OL-2611 stands, including the expiry.

subject: Re: Re: Offer: Senior Backend Engineer, Corvid
body: 192 works for me. I'm accepting, signed letter attached. I'll tell the other company this morning. Thank you both!
note: An acceptance stops the offer clock. High because the offer log still shows it open and needs updating, and the thread is a repeat.

subject: Pellham offer: a little more time?
body: Hi Nadia, I'm very keen on the controller role. Could Pellham give me until October 9 to decide? My partner is waiting on a relocation answer from his employer and I don't want to accept and then back out.
note: An extension request: the offer is expiring, so a clock runs, but its date is in the offer log under a reference she never quotes. October 9 is the date she wants, not the one that runs. No deadline is given, so a person sets it.

subject: OL-2615: Harriet's extension
body: Nadia, the offer committee can consider a short extension for Harriet at its September 30 meeting, but not before. Until then OL-2615 stands as written.
note: Due Oct 2, but the Pellham offer committee meets Sep 30 and the requisition waits on offer decisions: urgent from the schedule.

subject: Question on the offer letter
body: One question on the Pellham letter: does the 401k match start on day one, or after 90 days? The letter just says per plan documents.
note: A question about a live offer that raises no decision about its expiry: no clock. High because it names no logged offer.

subject: Offer for Sven
body: We'd like to offer Sven Halvorsen the DevOps role at 168 base plus the standard 10 percent bonus. Please extend it and give him until September 29 to decide. Happy to jump on a call with him if he has questions about on-call.
note: An instruction to extend an offer: nothing is running yet and the log has not seen it, so high rather than clocked.

subject: Re: Re: Offer for Sven
body: Has Sven signed yet? Our onboarding team is holding a laptop order on the countersigned letter.
note: A repeat chase from the client about an offer. The onboarding team is mentioned, but the ask is the signature.

subject: Re: Kestrel offer
body: I'm happy to accept. Signed letter attached. Can we talk start dates? I'd like to give notice at my current job on Monday and they usually want four weeks.
note: Three kinds in one reply: an acceptance for the recruiter, and a start-date question for the coordinator. The acceptance stops the offer clock, so no alert.

subject: Heads up
body: Heads up: my manager found out I'm interviewing and offered me a 15 percent retention raise. I still want to see the Corvid onsite through, but I wanted you to know before we get further.
note: A counteroffer from the candidate's current employer before any offer of ours exists. The offer class still holds it: it is about an offer, and it is the kind that loses placements.

subject: Closing out OL-2609
body: Quick housekeeping: Lindqvist formally declined, so we've closed OL-2609 in our system. Can you confirm it's closed on your side too?
note: Names a logged offer, but one already closed: no window is running and nothing needs logging.

subject: OL-2611 countersign
body: Tom, Farah says Corvid legal wants Elena's signed letter back before the 24th or they have to reissue it. I've put a reminder on OL-2611. Can you nudge her today?
note: Team mail, which is normally low and never a clock of its own. But it names an open offer in the log, the log corroborates the expiry, and the alert is right.

subject: Hybrid?
body: Quick question about the Brightwater role: is it hybrid, and if so how many days a week in the Leeds Street office?

subject: Corvid onsite
body: Hi Tom, following up on my onsite last Thursday. Any word from Corvid? I have some other conversations going and would like to know where I stand.
note: A candidate chasing: a repeat, so high.

subject: Resume: senior data engineer
body: Saw the Brightwater Data Engineer post on your site. Attaching my resume. Eight years on Spark and Airflow, currently at a freight broker, open to hybrid.
note: An applicant who is not in the contacts yet; the requisition is named in the text.

subject: Notice period
body: For planning: my notice period is four weeks, so the earliest I could start would be early November. I also have a week of leave booked in mid December.

subject: Thanks for today
body: Thanks for the call today! Really enjoyed hearing about the Brightwater team and the warehouse platform. One thing, no pressure at all: I have another process wrapping up and they've asked for my decision by Friday, so it would help to know where I stand with you.
note: Disguised: a friendly thank-you with a competing offer's deadline in its last sentence. If the firm misses it, the candidate is gone.

subject: Update from my side
body: Another company has made me an offer. They want an answer no later than September 28. Brightwater is still my first choice. Is there any chance of speeding things up?

subject: Shortlist timing
body: When should we expect the first CVs for the data engineer role? My VP asked this morning.
note: Client mail goes to the account owner, who on Brightwater is not the requisition's recruiter.

subject: Re: Re: Shortlist timing
body: Chasing this again. Your confirmation says SLA-0341 and my VP keeps asking what that means in days.
note: Due Oct 2 in the SLA tracker, and the shortlist presentation that day waits on client items: urgent from the schedule.

subject: SLA-0338 shortlist
body: Will we have the DevOps shortlist under SLA-0338 in time? I'd like to review it before the intake call for the new req.
note: The account owner on Kestrel is the director, so the route is one person.

subject: Second slate
body: Where are we on the second slate under SLA-0335? The panel is blocked out and I would rather not lose it.

subject: Analyst searches
body: It has been two weeks since we asked to open the two analyst roles and we haven't seen a single profile. Where are we?
note: A repeat chase with none of the repeat words and no Re: in the subject. The label says high; the code reads a first ask.

subject: Headcount approved
body: Good news: finance approved the data engineer headcount through Q1. We need someone in seat by November 16 to hit the warehouse migration, so that is our internal target.
note: The client's own business target, not a response clock the firm owes. A dated phrase parses, so expect a false alarm.

subject: New requisition: Site Reliability Engineer
body: Rosa has approved a second role, Site Reliability Engineer, same team and same terms as the DevOps search. Job description attached. We'd like to cover it in Wednesday's intake call.

subject: References for Harriet
body: Reminder that SLA-0343, the two reference reports on Harriet, are due to us Wednesday. The offer is conditional on them.

subject: Nice work on Sven
body: Great to have Sven over the line, thank you. Also great to see the SRE req live. Just flagging our team has an offsite at the end of the week, so the DevOps backfill list per SLA-0338 would be best in our inbox early. No stress!
note: Disguised: a thank-you note that names an open SLA item in its last lines. The tracker says Sep 25, and the intake call on Sep 23 waits on client items.

subject: FW: salary band question
body: Leah reached out to me directly on LinkedIn asking about the salary band and whether there is a signing bonus. Forwarding so your team handles it rather than me.
note: A candidate's question that arrives through the client. By the class rules it is the client writing, so it reaches the account owner, who passes it to the recruiter.

subject: Panel availability for the loop
body: Our panel can do Tuesday Sep 29 from 10 to 3. Please slot the three second-slate candidates in 45 minute blocks with a break at noon.

subject: Need to move my Corvid call
body: Something came up at work. Could we move Wednesday's call with the engineering manager to Thursday, same time? Sorry for the short notice.

subject: Screen times
body: For the Brightwater screen I can do Wednesday at 4 or Thursday morning before 10. Video or phone both fine.

subject: Loop on the 29th: names please
body: Please confirm the three second-slate names for the Sep 29 loop by Thursday. I need to release the panel otherwise, and getting six engineers back in one room took a month.
note: A panel hold that lapses if unconfirmed is a clock: the slot is lost.

subject: Leah's second interview
body: Can we push Leah's second interview to next week? Our lead engineer is out sick. Any afternoon except Friday.

subject: Accepted: Jonah Pierce technical screen
body: Rosa Delgado has accepted this invitation. Jonah Pierce technical screen, Kestrel Health, Wed Sep 23 2:00pm to 3:00pm, video link in the invite.
note: An automated calendar notice: scheduling only, not the client writing.

subject: Tomorrow's interview
body: Hi, I'm so sorry but I have to cancel tomorrow's interview, family emergency. Can we reschedule for later in the week?
note: Names no client and the sender is not in the contacts. Scheduling reaches the coordinator by name; the candidate half has no requisition, so a person decides whose it is.

subject: Panel hold: Jonah Pierce
body: We're holding the Thursday panel for Jonah Pierce, pending a good technical screen. Please confirm by Wednesday or we release the room and the interviewers.

subject: Thursday!
body: Really looking forward to Thursday's panel at Kestrel, thanks for setting it up. Their front desk emailed to say I have to return the signed visitor NDA before Wednesday or they can't admit me to the building, so I've sent it straight back. Do you need a copy?
note: Disguised: an excited candidate note with a precondition for the panel in the middle. Miss it and the panel is lost.

subject: Consent done
body: Just completed the consent form for the background check. Anything else I need before the 28th?
note: Consent is done, so the cutoff is met: no clock.

subject: Start confirmation: Marcus Cole
body: Confirming Marcus Cole's first day: Monday September 28, 9am, reception on level 4. He'll spend the morning with IT and meet Priya at noon.
note: Client HR writing only about a placed hire's start: onboarding, not client mail.

subject: Screening complete
body: Screening complete for Marcus Cole. Result: clear. The full report is available in your Clearline account.

subject: Start date
body: Kestrel said October 19 works for them. I gave notice this morning. What paperwork do I need from my side?

subject: Drug screen for Sven Halvorsen
body: We've ordered Sven's pre-employment drug screen today. It must be completed within 5 business days of the order at any listed collection site.

subject: Welcome lunch for Marcus
body: Welcome lunch for Marcus is booked, thank you for such a smooth process! One small thing: payroll needs his signed direct deposit form and W-4 no later than September 25 to make the first pay run, so do pass that on.
note: Disguised: a warm thank-you with a payroll cutoff in the middle.

subject: Re: Start date paperwork
body: Got the I-9 document list, thanks Ben. I'll bring my passport.

subject: FW: background check link
body:
Marcus emailed me directly about this, forwarding so your team can sort it.

---- Forwarded ----
Hi Priya, the Clearline link I was sent has expired and I can't complete the consent. Can someone resend it?
note: Disguised and through the wrong sender: the hiring manager forwards a placed candidate's problem. The consent cutoff is running but the forward gives no date, so a person sets it.

subject: ONB-0212: I-9 appointment
body: Confirming Marcus Cole's I-9 Section 2 review with our HR desk at 8:30 on his first day, per your checklist ONB-0212. He needs an unexpired passport, or a List B and List C pair.

subject: Order CL-7738: consent needed
body: Sven Halvorsen has been invited to complete consent for order CL-7738. Consent must be completed within 7 days of the invitation or the order is cancelled.
note: A new order the onboarding tracker has not logged yet; the window is in the text.

subject: Invoice CJ-55012
body: Invoice CJ-55012 for your September job slots: 12 slots, $1,840.00, due by October 15. Pay online or by ACH.
note: A bill's due date is the firm's calendar, not a response clock.

subject: Remittance: FT-2291R
body: Payment of FT-2291R, the reissued placement fee invoice at 22 percent, was sent by ACH today.

subject: Rejected: invoice FT-2275
body: Invoice FT-2275 for the Nakamura placement was rejected by our AP system: it is missing PO number CRV-PO-7781. Please resubmit with the PO on the face of the invoice.

subject: Analyst guarantee
body: Bad news, I'm afraid. Devin Pratt, the analyst you placed with us in July, resigned yesterday, which is week 9 of the 90-day guarantee. Per our agreement please confirm the replacement search within 10 business days.
note: A guarantee claim is a clock: the replacement must be confirmed inside the agreement's window.

subject: Fee terms
body: Before our committee signs off on the controller, can you confirm the fee is 20 percent of first-year base and the guarantee is 90 days? Our auditors ask.

subject: Your plan renews soon
body: Your annual Crewpost Pro plan renews on October 1 at $6,200. To change or cancel, notify us within 14 days of this notice.
note: A window on a vendor's bill. It is the firm's own calendar with a supplier, not a response clock it owes anyone.

subject: Invoice CS-2209
body: Invoice CS-2209 attached: six background checks in September at $58 each, net 30.

subject: Re: Re: Invoice FT-2291: query
body: Still waiting on the reissued invoice at 22 percent. We can't release payment until it arrives.
note: A repeat chase, but repeats raise only client and candidate mail. Accounts payable on an invoice is billing and stays normal.

subject: Loop feedback, and one other thing
body:
Thanks for getting the Vasquez offer moving so quickly.

Unrelated: Mateo Nakamura, who you placed with us in July, has resigned effective October 9. I believe that falls inside your 90-day guarantee, and our agreement says the replacement search starts within 5 business days of notice, so please treat this as notice.
note: Disguised: a guarantee notice in the second paragraph of a feedback email. The window counts business days from the notice.

subject: Re: Jonah's screen, and an invoice
body: Jonah's screen is confirmed for the 23rd. Separately, our AP says your invoice FT-2290 for Priyan Das's placement is missing a PO, so it is sitting in their queue.
note: Three owners in one short reply: the account owner, the coordinator and accounts. No clock in any of them.

subject: 15 minutes to see Quillsource?
body: Hi there, Quillsource finds passive engineers your competitors miss. Could I grab 15 minutes next week for a demo?

subject: Featured slots 30% off, ends Friday
body: Boost your listings to the top of search. Featured slots are 30% off, offer ends Friday. Upgrade in one click from your dashboard.
note: A pitch from a vendor the firm pays, with a date that parses. The date is the vendor's calendar.

subject: ACTION REQUIRED: EEO registry listing
body: Our records show your agency is not listed in the Workforce Registry. Employers must maintain a current listing. The deadline is October 5. Complete your listing for $395 at the link below. This is not a government agency.
note: A pitch dressed as a regulatory notice, with a deadline. The small print says what it is.

subject: Split-fee partnership?
body: We have three strong finance candidates who would suit your clients. Open to a 50/50 split on placements? Happy to share profiles under NDA.
note: Another agency proposing a split: unsolicited.

subject: Early bird: Staffing Growth Summit
body: Join 800 agency owners in Austin this November. Early bird pricing ends by September 30.

subject: Never take interview notes again
body: Tallyboard joins your candidate calls, writes the summary and pushes it to your ATS. Free for your first 20 interviews.

subject: 2026 salary benchmarks for engineering roles
body: Download our 2026 engineering salary benchmark report, free for agencies. See where backend, data and DevOps offers are landing this quarter.

subject: Contractors in 40 countries
body: Place contractors anywhere without setting up an entity. Rostermint handles payroll, compliance and benefits.

subject: Background checks in 24 hours
body: Tired of checks holding up start dates? Ashgrove turns most checks around in 24 hours. Switch this month and your first 10 are free.
note: A screening vendor the firm does not use, selling: a pitch, not onboarding.

subject: 5 candidates matched to your Data Engineer opening
body: We found 5 candidates who match your open Data Engineer role. Unlock their contact details with a Quillsource subscription.
note: Reads like a candidate submission and names a role the firm is working, but it is a sourcing tool selling access.

subject: Your offer is ready
body: Your exclusive offer is ready: 3 months of Networkly Recruiter free, then 20% off. Claim it before it disappears.
note: Subject says offer. It is not a job offer.

subject: Your agency website
body: Your site loads in 6.2 seconds on mobile. We build fast sites for recruiting agencies. Free audit?

subject: 2 million resumes, one search
body: Search 2 million resumes by skill, location and salary. Agency plans from $299 a month.

subject: Invoice #88213: Premium Employer Listing
body: Invoice #88213. Premium Employer Listing, annual: $489.00. This is not a bill. This is a solicitation. You are under no obligation to pay unless you accept this offer.
note: A pitch dressed as an invoice; the small print says so.

subject: Webinar: stop losing candidates to counteroffers
body: Counteroffers kill 1 in 4 placements. Join our free webinar Thursday to learn the five scripts top recruiters use to close.
note: About counteroffers, but a vendor webinar, not an offer matter.

subject: Meeting rooms for candidate interviews
body: Need a neutral room for candidate interviews? Deskhaven rooms from $25 an hour, bookable in minutes.
note: A pitch that mentions interviews: not scheduling.

subject: Vasquez call
body: Calling Elena at 8 tonight about the Corvid base. I think 192 closes it. Will update the thread after.

subject: Cover my Halden call?
body: Tom, can you cover my Halden check-in Wednesday at 3? I'll be at the Pellham office. Notes are in the ATS.

subject: September fees
body: Aisha, September fees billed so far: three placements, one reissue pending with Halden AP. Corvid's Nakamura invoice needs a PO before it will pay.
note: Accounts talking to the director about fees: team mail, not a billing item to route.

subject: Updated fee agreement template
body: I've updated the fee agreement template with the new guarantee wording. Please use v7 for anything going out from today.

subject: PTO requests
body: Please send any time off you're planning for Q4 by October 2 so I can plan interview cover.
note: Internal mail with a dated phrase that parses. It is the team's calendar, not a clock.

subject: FW: Analyst searches
body: Nadia, Halden again on the analyst roles, see below. Want me to pull the two treasury profiles from my pipeline?

subject: Cole invoice timing
body: Heads up that the Cole placement invoice goes out on his start date, so I'll need the confirmed first-day salary from Nadia.
